# Pixar’s ‘Soul’ wins best animated feature Academy Award

Associated Press

Published: April 25, 2021 at 9:37 PM Updated: April 26, 2021 at 12:20 AM

Tags: Arts , Tina Fey , entertainment , Jamie Foxx

Full Screen 1 / 3

Previous photo

Next photo
Dana Murray, left, and Pete Docter, winners of the award for animated feature film for "Soul," pose in the press room at the Oscars on Sunday, April 25, 2021, at Union Station in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello, Pool) Dana Murray, left, and Pete Docter, winners of the award for animated feature film for "Soul," pose in the press room at the Oscars on Sunday, April 25, 2021, at Union Station in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello, Pool) Dana Murray, left, and Pete Docter, winners of the award for animated feature film for "Soul," pose in the press room at the Oscars on Sunday, April 25, 2021, at Union Station in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello, Pool)

Dana Murray, left, and Pete Docter, winners of the award for animated feature film for "Soul," pose in the press room at the Oscars on Sunday, April 25, 2021, at Union Station in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Chris Pizzello, Pool)
**LOS ANGELES** – Pixar’s “Soul” has won the heart of Oscar voters, continuing the Disney division’s dominance in the best animated feature category.

Sunday night's victory gave Pixar 11 wins in the 20 years since the category was established.

Recommended Videos

* * *

Directed by Pete Docter and featuring the voices of Jamie Foxx and Tina Fey, “Soul” follows a middle school band teacher who dreams of being a jazz musician and tries to escape the afterlife to do it.

“This film started as a love letter to jazz, but we had no idea how much jazz would teach us about life,” said Docter, who accepted the Oscar with producer Dana Murray. “We don’t get to control what happens. But we can, like a jazz musician, turn whatever happens into something of value and something of beauty.”

Docter praised music and art teachers everywhere, including his parents for making the world a “better place.”

![](https://insidethemagic.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/Coco-800x400.jpg)
Disney-Pixar’s “Coco” is the latest in a long line of successful movies from the animation studio, and the 2018 Academy Awards further validated that. The hit film took home the Oscars for ‘Best Animated Feature’ and ‘Best Original Song’ for “Remember Me.”

The Academy Award for’Best Animated Feature’ was the second for director Lee Unkrich, who also won for his work on “Toy Story 3.” It was also the sixth consecutive Disney film to win the award. In fact, since the award was created in 2001, Disney films have earned 12 of the 17 awards. Pixar films have accounted for nine of those.

**WATCH – “COCO” STAR ANTHONY GONZALEZ PERFORMS “REMEMBER ME”:**  

“Remember Me” was written by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez, who also took home the award in 2013 for “Let It Go.” You can see the song performed by “Coco” star Anthony Gonzalez in the video above.

This was the third time a Disney film has earned this honor in the past eight years.
“Let It Go” from “Frozen” won the award in 2013, and “We Belong Together” from “Toy Story 3” won it in 2010.
